summary: HR AC-13 in-memory storage seam reference adapter records employment lifecycle, labor workflow, leave payroll-impact, and sensitive-read metadata with idempotency validation while explicitly avoiding durable storage, sensitive-data retrieval, Workflow execution, Payroll calls, and audit-chain emission claims.

findings: The adapter is a compact BTreeMap/BTreeSet reference implementation with no provider configuration or hidden I/O.
Malformed idempotency keys and duplicate writes fail deterministically before records are inserted.
The storage port separates HR metadata record semantics from future durable Postgres/RLS or cloud provider adapters.
Capability flags keep durable backend, Postgres/RLS, sensitive data retrieval, Workflow execution, Payroll network calls, and audit emission false until real integrations land.

F3_adversarial.failing_fixture_id: duplicate idempotency and malformed key tests
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if duplicate writes are accepted, malformed keys reserve, HR envelope metadata is dropped, or capability flags imply durable storage/sensitive data retrieval/runtime execution.
findings: Positive coverage persists all four HR record kinds; negative coverage refuses duplicate idempotency keys and unsafe key shapes.
The crate exposes a named storage port trait, in-memory store, stored-record shape, capability descriptor, and explicit persist helpers for each existing HR app envelope.
HR storage adapter tests/clippy, HR package-group tests/clippy, 19-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, data_class scan, and quality-marker scan passed.

alternatives_named: store sensitive HR data in the reference adapter
add an in-memory HR metadata storage seam reference first
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The in-memory reference pins idempotency and HR envelope-to-record contracts before durable storage, RLS, and cloud operations exist.
rejected_reasons: Postgres/RLS requires migrations, tenancy controls, rollback, and SLO evidence that are outside this slice.
Storing or retrieving sensitive HR data would overclaim privacy/security posture; this adapter records metadata only.

findings: No secrets, provider credentials, databases, or network clients are introduced.
Idempotency key validation rejects empty, whitespace, path traversal, and duplicate keys; sensitive-data retrieval capability remains false.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No durable backend exists; tests exercise fixed-size in-memory metadata records.

findings.summary: Operations are bounded by BTreeMap/BTreeSet key operations over in-process metadata; no network, filesystem, or database I/O is introduced.

findings: Stored-record and capability public fields carry data_class annotations.
Capability response explicitly marks durable backend, Postgres/RLS, sensitive data retrieval, Workflow execution, Payroll calls, and audit-chain emission false.
The change is additive: one HR in-memory adapter crate, catalog row, workspace membership, spec/tasks/evidence updates, and no migrations or external resources.
Stored records carry topic, tenant, legal entity, primary ref, idempotency key, schema version, payload data class, evidence count, and backend label for future audit/telemetry labels.
HR AC-13 and D-15 record the storage seam while durable storage, Postgres/RLS, sensitive-data retrieval, Workflow execution, Payroll calls, and cloud/SLO evidence remain future slices.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A storage seam reference can land before durable HR storage if it is explicitly volatile, metadata-only, and all provider/runtime capabilities stay false.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: specs/microservices/hr.json AC-13 and HR storage capability tests
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Future durable HR adapters would lack a tested idempotency and metadata record-shape contract for lifecycle, labor workflow, leave payroll-impact, and sensitive-read policy envelopes.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Shared storage providers do not define HR-specific metadata repository semantics or privacy non-claims.

findings: This advances HR toward later Oyatie cloud integration without pretending a durable HR datastore, sensitive data retrieval path, Workflow engine, or Payroll network integration exists.
Names follow HR employment storage adapter, in-memory, idempotency, and metadata record vocabulary.
HR spec, plan, todo, evidence, catalog, and audit-chain references were updated.
Storage-specific code lives in a new HR adapter crate; runtime/API/app/domain behavior remains unchanged.
No database migration, provider SDK, HTTP framework, runtime write integration, Workflow client, Payroll client, cloud adapter, or audit emitter was introduced.
No third-party dependencies were added; the crate depends only on existing HR app/domain crates.
Stored records include schema_version and stable topic/idempotency/reference fields; no wire API schema is changed.
Persistence helpers deterministically map existing HR app envelopes into record views and then enforce key validation/duplicate checks before insert.
